utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The proceedings will continue under Rule 15 bis in the absence of Judge Williams, on account of personal reasons. Cross-examination is continuing, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jasarevic. Yesterday, when we were talking, we also discussed the incident when -- involving three civilians in a civilian vehicle were seriously injured by reserve policemen. You said that you arrived immediately after the event occurred. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In connection with that event, I have only two more questions. Did you then find out -- were you informed that the reserve policemen who had shot the civilian, the civilian automobile, were Izetbegovic Adis and Sead [Realtime transcript read in error "Safet"] Srna?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see who shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A correction. Srna Sead. I said Srna Sead not Srna Safet, as it has been entered in the transcript. This is the correction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that after that event, Izetbegovic Adis, and Srna Sead fled to the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they fled to the Republic of Croatia. Possibly they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to -- P129 ter be placed in front of the witness. I notice that this statement is not in front of the witness, so I would kindly ask for it to be placed in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 4, item 19. Did you find it? Page 4, paragraph 19. Did you find it? Thank you. Here you claim, in the last sentence, that the Serb forces also blew up the bridge over Sava five months before the attack on Bosanski Samac, as well as downed the power lines. The Serbs themselves were saying publicly that they had done this. This is your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: As here you have used the expression "the Serb forces," I would ask you to explain to the Trial Chamber what you understand under -- with this term "Serb forces."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment and the then JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jasarevic, you were not a witness of the blowing up of the bridge over the river Sava?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You don't even know the exact date when this event took place?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with my assertion that this event took place on the 5th of February, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is the fact known to you that at the time - it means in the course of 1992 - that this bridge over the river Sava was protected by the special police forces of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which forces, but I do know that these were forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bosnian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You also stated here that the Serbs themselves publicly claimed that they had done this. Can you tell us here, in the Trial Chamber, the names and surnames of those Serbs who were boasting that they blew up the bridge?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall, but I remember that while I was in prison in Brcko, that they were saying how they blew up the bridge, as well as downed the power lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, please let us move to item 20 and -- on page 5. In item 20, you claim, the last sentence: "The people of the 4th Detachment were the checkpoint Crkvina and I knew these people myself personally"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you say who were these people for whom you knew that were members of the 4th Detachment and were the checkpoint in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Simo Vladic [as interpreted] and others, who were in uniforms and were the checkpoint in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please -- could you tell this Trial Chamber how far is the village of Crkvina far from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is five kilometres from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that Miko Sucin and Tesic Cvikan, that they lived in Samac, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with my claim that they were members of another [as interpreted] detachment of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to which they belonged, but they were always in the Cafe AS, and it was from there that they went on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have one clarification for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Pisarevic said: "Would you agree that they were members --" well, here it's stated "another detachment" in the transcript. Actually, what Mr. Pisarevic said, if they were members of 2nd Detachment. In our language, it is the same: "Second" and "another" is the same word for it. But in this situation the meaning of this was the 2nd Detachment, so it's just that clarification for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. That will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you determine, give a time frame, if you can recall, when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the month of January, February, March, beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Which event? What happened?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this -- at the checkpoint I said I couldn't remember this all took place ten years ago. However, I did see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel, do remember to pause, because the record does get confused. When the witness is answering, pause after he has finished so that the interpretation is completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall attempt to do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please look at item 24 of your statement, and in the last line you said -- you stated that you're not a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you, a year earlier, in April 1991, sign the enrollment slip for the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've signed no application whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, in the police station, on the 26th of April, 1992, say to Inspector Savic, during the interrogation, did you say that somewhere in April 1991 that you signed an application for SDA, that you signed that in a state of intoxication, and that your wife had then torn up this application form at home?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It appears from counsel's question that he is referring to a very specific document. He can tell us the date, who the alleged statement taker was, and the contents. To the best of my knowledge, we don't have that document, and if Defence counsel have it and are using it, they've never disclosed it to us, although they are engaged in the procedure of reciprocal discovery. So I would like to get clarification from Defence counsel if they do in fact have this document. It would appear from the question Mr. Pisarevic is quoting from, or at least selecting information from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pisarevic, is it a document or are these your instructions from your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are the instructions I received from not my client but my investigators, who, from the inspector Milos Savic stated -- who claims that Mr. Jasarevic stated that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, you do know that I do not drink alcohol [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I never claimed. I only asked whether you stated that or not.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that situation, I signed and stated whatever they asked me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Reidy. Is there any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I didn't give you permission, and you're asking -- Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Yes. Yes. Sorry. Can I proceed, Your Honour? It's a clarification in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's page 6, line 20. Witness said: "Yes." And then: "However, you do know that I do not drink alcohol." So it was "yes" and then "however." I don't want to seek with any clarification what the witness said. We have everything on the audiotape, so we can do that afterwards. It's just for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, please clarify the answer which the witness gave with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, Witness, you gave such a statement to Milos Savic, but you had to do that.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that you do not drink.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't drink, and I never got intoxicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, will that suffice?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's okay, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And now let us turn to paragraph 25, where you speak about the organisation of guards and about the incident which happened in the Valentino Cafe. Yes, that was it, wasn't it? Can we agree that the area where the Muslims lived in the municipality of Samac, that it was only the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that Muslims organised their guards and patrols only in the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the event in Cafe Valentino.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And which, according to you, happened in February 1992.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And you also mentioned the expression that in that cafe, Enver Bobic and Mensur Hadzialijagic were killed there.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it was translated, and later in my statement I say that they activated the hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that it happened as an accident?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that this event happened on the 14th of February, 1992? It is somewhere in the middle of February?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I already mentioned about these dates ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, on that occasion there was also -- another person was seriously wounded, namely, Pavlovic Gordana, a Serb woman, who was the girlfriend of Bobic Enver?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I spoke only about the dead, and there was more -- there were a few people wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You were in front of the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: There, in front of the police station in Bosanski Samac, many people have gathered, mainly members from the Muslim ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were many people there, but I don't know what about the people from the 4th Detachment. People of all ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that then many who were present of the inhabitants there publicly accused Serbs and the JNA?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what was happening in front of the SUP. As far as the rest goes, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I'm asking you what was happening in front of the SUP, where you were.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the event on the basis of which the 4th Detachment would take over the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were they accused or weren't they accused?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, on that occasion you were publicly speaking in front of the public that Serbs and the JNA had perpetrated that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never stated that. It's not the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: According to my sources of information, you, on that occasion, went up the steps of the staircase of the police station and you publicly spoke out against Serbs and the JNA, and also invited for the people to go against these -- the Serbs and JNA.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an ordinary provocation, and it's a lie. It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, were you standing on the stairs of the police station together with Paradzic Blaz?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see Paradzic Blaz. I was together with Nusret Hadzijusufovic and I don't know whether I was on the steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So you claim that on that occasion, you did not curse the Serbs' mothers, you did not call them Chetniks, and did not call people to rally against Serbs and the JNA?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that. You know who were my friends in Samac? Yes. All my friends in my boyhood days were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem with the transcript recording. Because instead of question, you know who were my friends from Samac, I thought that's what the witness said. Can we clear this, Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just clarify your statement, previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that your friends in your youth were mainly Serbs.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, has that been clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: As you were there on the spot, can you confirm the fact that this situation in front of the police station in Bosanski Samac calmed down when Hadzialijagic Safet, known as Coner, came out of the police building and addressed the people who rallied there and stated by -- and when he stated that the police is doing its work and when he asked everyone to go peacefully home?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I quoted everything. Who shouted Ustashas --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, in my statement, also said that I knew that nobody had thrown the bomb, and Coner only confirmed that. I didn't say anything else in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: However, in your statement -- speak that [as interpreted] -- you talked in front of the SUP building with Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did. We talked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Slowly. However, Mr. Zaric claims that he did not talk to you at all that evening. Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer with a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You've clarified it in your statement, but give me a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the statement, it is clearly stated what kind of a talk we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has said that he spoke with Mr. Zaric. That's his story. He says both on the record and in his statement what passed between him and Mr. Zaric. If Mr. Zaric disagrees with us, that's a matter for the Defence. But it is not for the counsel to put what Mr. Zaric -- saying Mr. Zaric claimed he didn't talk to you at all that evening, yes or no? How does the witness supposed to help us on what Mr. Zaric tells counsel? It's very clear what the witness's position is. So to ask him to say whether or not Mr. Zaric would confirm that is beyond the witness's capacity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. I think it's the way it's handled as -- when you're confronting a witness with what your instructions are. I think that was the problem. Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You, Mr. Jasarevic, gave a statement to the Prosecution on the 3rd, 4th, and 5th of February, 1995, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In that statement, you stated -- you talked about this event, but nowhere did you mention that you had talked with Mr. Simo Zaric. I will not continue to question you about this, but I would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, Your Honours, say a few words to my distinguished colleagues from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: About --? Oh, I see. Yes, you can go ahead. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Office of the Prosecution confirm the statement that in his statement, Mr. Jasarevic never spoke about this event that is in his statement made on February 3, 4, and 5, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, let me tell you what's in the statement and let the Bench assess it itself about this matter, bearing in mind that when I went back to take the interview in 2001, that is -- I'll tell you what's in the statement. It says: "Before the war, Muslims organised neighbourhood guards or controlled areas near where they lived. Croats did this too to some extent. In a coffee shop once, two young men were killed by a bomb. This prompted the Muslims and Croats living in the area to organise themselves to protect their living areas." I simply explored that further with the witness last May as it became an issue in this trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel. This is the quotation you are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. This is exactly what I wanted to do. I didn't want this statement to be read to the witness. What I wanted to put to you is the following: In this statement, in no item did Mr. Jasarevic mention that he talked to or that he was in front of the SUP and ever had a conversation with Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear from the quotation by Ms. Reidy. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Page 12, line 25, for the record, Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic never received the statement from 2001, and I would like to see a clarification from the -- our learned friends from Prosecution. Because we have only 1995 statement and 2002, so it seems to me that it's something a little bit odd. What's actually is.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, it's May 2002. I've mis-spoken, I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't understand. Mr. Pantelic's request -- submission is that they never received this statement from which Mr. Pisarevic is quoting.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, no. I'm sorry, Your Honour. Just before it goes off the screen, you'll see I said when I went back to take the interview in 2001. I meant the interview 2002, May 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic is now trying to insinuate from my transcript error that I went back and I've had another statement taken in 2001, which wasn't disclosed. There are two statements from Mr. Jasarevic, there's the one from 1995 and the one in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. All you needed was to explain, because Mr. Pantelic misunderstood from the way it was put.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Everything is possible during trial proceedings, Your Honour. You know we are the witness here. There are many statements. So I don't know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, you gave this statement. You had already confirmed it. And you made this statement on the basis of your knowledge and recollection; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how come that you have now been able to come up with new knowledge ten years after the event took place? And I'm referring to this new knowledge, namely, about this conversation with Mr. Zaric, and you had no knowledge of this discussion eight years and two months after the conversation itself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask counsel to rephrase the question. This knowledge, he's saying it's new knowledge. It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- new element to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If that's what you're trying to explain, let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my statement, I mentioned that I was there, which had also been confirmed, and that I saw all these events, that I heard it. It was only in greater detail that I described this particular event.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you do that on February 3, 4, and 5, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] They're asking him why didn't you do --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry. They're asking him why he didn't take a certain action. In order for them to ask that question first, they have to ask: Was there any discussion about that particular incident? We see from the 1995 statement that he gave a generalised discussion. The next question should be if there was any further discussion relating to that particular incident, which they haven't asked. If they then ask that second question, then they can get to the third question, which is: Why, when they asked you about that particular incident, did you not say those specific things back then? But they're jumping -- they're actually assuming that there was some specific questions concerning that incident and that he failed to answer those back then. There is no evidence, number one, that there was any discussion concerning the Valentino Cafe other than those general references that the examiner didn't come back and say, "Well, let's talk about this" and then ask specific questions. You can't ask a person why they didn't say something if they weren't questioned about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In fairness to the Defence, Mr. Weiner, the Defence is right in assuming that if any matter concerning that event was touched upon, then the witness perhaps would have given further details. And the witness is in a position to answer whether he was asked about the details or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's -- I totally agree, Your Honour. That's what I feel the next question is. They've gone to a third question? The first question is: You were asked about what happened back then. He said, "Yes, there were several incidents that occurred." The second question is Your Honour's question, where they were asked further details and then you ask the person: Why didn't you give that answer back then? They did not ask if there was any follow-up questions concerning that. They've already gone to the third question, which isn't being fair to the witness. Because now you're almost accusing him of being a liar, which is not fair --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think you are stretching it too far. I think in fairness to the Defence, let them ask such a question and let the witness explain. The witness was there at the interview. The witness was there at the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So let him explain why he didn't give that detail. He's capable of doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you must have had a better recollection in 1995 than you do in the year 2002; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this incident, may I remind you of some other events? Do you remember that a meeting of the local population was held in the cinema hall in Bosanski Samac in connection with this misfortunate killing of the two young men, the injuring of this girl, and others, as you mentioned it before?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I was not attending this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my next question. So you did not attend this meeting of the citizens?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us proceed to item 27 now. In this item, you stated: "We couldn't see the police; therefore, we decided to do something on our own to protect ourselves." Did I read this out correctly?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I will now put a few questions to you in connection with this statement. First, can you confirm that the head of the police in Bosanski Samac at that time was Mr. Vinko Dragicevic, of Croat ethnicity? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact to me that at that time the chief of the criminal department in the police in Bosanski Samac was Dragan Lukac, of Croat ethnicity, from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell this Honourable Chamber: Under this term, we decided, do you understand under this term the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The citizens of Bosanski Samac who decided to undertake certain measures in the local community of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And you said a meeting was held of all people. Are you referring to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the local community where people of all ethnic backgrounds lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me when approximately this meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The month, perhaps, the year?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after these incidents. I don't really know. Maybe a month before Samac fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who organised this meeting and who signed the invitation to attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no written invitations. I received no invitation in writing whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who, in fact, sent out the invitation to attend this meeting in the local commune?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who sent out this invitation to attend the meeting in the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who chaired and led the discussion in this meeting in the local commune?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was general chaos. Everybody took the floor. Everybody spoke. I really do not know who was supposed to chair it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I understand you well. In other words, are you saying that you do not know who was chairing and leading the discussion in the course of this meeting held in the local commune?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Fitozovic did it. In fact, we understood it that he was representing the SDA; therefore, I decided that only the hunters, on their own, will organise themselves and protect the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned this hunters' association, so my next question goes as follows: Was this a municipal organisation? Wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be show Exhibit D25/4 ter. Would the usher please show this exhibit to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please turn to Exhibit 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness should be shown the correct -- yes, the correct page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exhibit or attachment 8. The page is not numbered, but it says on top "exhibit" or "attachment 8."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it is attachment 8?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Could you please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough, Witness, to read the title on this attachment.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Read aloud, would you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Department of hunters."

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you now read the next line, please, where it says "commander," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are the lists that you prepared. We never had a list like that. In my statement, I explained the circumstances relevant to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I simply asked you to read out what is said here.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it out for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You read only the first line. You didn't read the second line on this document.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Department of hunters."

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What is next?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Commander Jasarevic, Hasan." I told you before that you were putting together these lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this phone number here the phone number that belonged to Jasarevic Hasan?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have the phone book, and you could check the phone book and take this phone number out of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, just answer the questions as put to you by counsel, that's all. Do not say anything else. Just answer the questions put to you by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How did you come to this conclusion that somebody else prepared this list?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there were no lists. I explained it in my statement how the meeting was held. There were no lists and there were no phone numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the following: Is this the phone number that belonged to Mr. Jasarevic Hasan?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we then agree that Mr. Jasarevic Hasan is your brother?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we, very quickly, browse through these names from 1 to 9, and then it says "the reserve." Just check the names. You don't have to read them. Have you seen them?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that all persons under items 1 through 9, and all persons mentioned under the reserve, items 1 to 2, are persons of Muslim background?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me put one more question to you in connection with this. Mr. Jasarevic Hasan was the president of the municipal organisation of hunters, known as Fazan, in Bosanski Samac? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not need this exhibit any more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now focus on item 28 of your statement. Here it says: "I was a member of this neighbourhood guard..." And so on and so forth, something about the weapons and arms. In relation to your statement in item 28, I will put a few questions to you. How did you become a member of the neighbourhood guard?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I explained the way in which I became a member of the neighbourhood guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you become a member of the neighbourhood guard following our knowledge and our information -- you had to be a member of an armed unit for the defence of the city, the commander of which was Alija Fitozovic. Are you familiar with the existence of such a unit?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about it, but I was not its member.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be given Exhibit D14/4 ter. Could this exhibit be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, would you please have a look at this document and read the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, the exhibits which have already been discussed, whose titles have been read and interpreted, we should not repeat that. The witness can read the title to himself, right, so that he familiarises himself with what the document contains and then you can go ahead with your questions. We shall move much faster that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honours. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You have seen this document, Witness. Could you please have a look at the document in front of you, and to pay particular attention to the ethnic structure of persons whose names figure on this document. Have you seen it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that on this list we have predominantly members of the Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, it doesn't say anything as to who prepared this list, who signed the list. Anybody could have drafted this list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Mr. Pisarevic -- I'm sorry. Witness -- Mr. Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just answer the questions put to you by counsel. I've given you this warning before. Do not assume anything, just answer the questions put to you by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You understood this warning. Once again, are persons on this list predominantly members of the Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to turn to the second page of this document and to focus on number 34, where it says Jasarevic Osman, Bulevar Revolucije. Is this your first and family name?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I no longer need this document, usher. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You have stated that Safet Srna brought you an automatic rifle with a clip of ammunition and that Srna Safet is the brother of Srna Senad [as interpreted]; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber under whose orders and whose approval Srna Safet brought you that automatic rifle and a clip of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I said that I don't know at whose orders and that I also returned the rifle to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the document D38/1 to be presented to the witness and, at the same time, also evidence D35/1. Please place these two documents on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please look at this document. On this document, under number 10, we have the name Jasarevic Osman.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 40 bullets, 40 rounds of ammo in a clip, 45 armour piercing, and 30 tracer. 40 rounds cannot be placed in a clip, and in my statement I said that I received an automatic rifle and one clip of ammo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you were not -- you did not receive this ammunition that is written here?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So these are -- it's ammunition for automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what is this, and I don't know who wrote down my name in order for issuing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now please place the document D35/1 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to look at the second page and under number 31. Will you agree that under 31 we have Jasarevic Osman? And concerning the type of weapons, it's ditto because under 30, Nurkic Ajdin it says Kalashnikov, that you received so many rounds of ammunition, quantity 115 and 4 clips. Did I read out this correctly?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in this last column where -- the last column, you have comments that the weapon has been returned or given to somebody else, there's nothing like that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said I received a rifle and one clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to that last assertion by Defence counsel. The last right hand column has no heading of it indicating what sort of comments or anything that should be entered in there. Now I see something say, "at the MUP", "from Aziz". It means nothing. It doesn't mean they were returned. I think I can see only one entry where someone says returned to Sarajevo against -- it's not against any name. So the counsel is saying there's entries in the right hand column commenting that weapons have been returned or given to someone else, and they don't exist on the document that I'm now looking at. So it's a misleading question. It's not what the document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought that counsel was simply putting it to the witness that across your name there are no comments to show that the --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: He actually says: "Do you agree that in this last column, you have comments that the weapon has been returned or given to someone else?" And we don't have, in the right hand column, those sort of comments at all. Yes, he does --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see--

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But he's suggesting that the others have comments and his has nothing and those aren't the comments that are in the right hand columns. So it's misleading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's clarify this, Mr. Pisarevic. I think it gets more confused. Can you put the question to the witness again? Perhaps rephrase your question so that it is clear as to what you're asking the witness regarding the entries on that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, under number 31, we find your name and surname, and in the last column, there no entry has been made?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that next to some names contained on this list, in the last column, some observations have been entered?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some observations exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, have we clarified this issue? Ms. Reidy, is it clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely. And that's fine. But there are no comments that guns are returned except --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The questions were put and the answers are clear, so you can proceed, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you, after this, do you still claim that you were not armed with an automatic weapon known as a Kalashnikov? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In my statement, it says what kind of a rifle I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to clarify that a bit, because I have a feeling it will not be faithfully presented in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that you received an automatic weapon. You did not say the name, the mark of that automatic rifle, whether it was of a Yugoslav make, Russian make, Romanian, Chinese.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these are certain types of Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we therefore agree that also an automatic rifle that you received was also a type of Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The automatic rifle I received was of the Yugoslav National Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now the evidence D39/1 be presented to the witness. The previous documents do not serve me any more. Please remove them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at this evidence, and particularly to focus your attention to the group 4, group 4. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the group going under number 4 consists of Tihic Pasaga, from Samac; the second member of the group, we find your name, Jasarevic Osman; and as the third member, is Seljakovic Hajrudin, also known as Mrki, and from Samac? Did I read that out correctly?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And now please look at all of these groups, and can you confirm that all the persons mentioned here are practically all of them of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please turn the second page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please just glance at this list of the patrol groups.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that also the persons in the consisting -- comprising the patrols from P1 to P6 are all of Muslim ethnicity, from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you have mentioned that you went in the neighbourhood guard with Fitozovic Smail, an economist, who was the director of the Mebos from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a retired director of the Mebos factory. He was already -- he was a retiree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: But he was director of the Mebos, the Mebos where you were also employed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that in the company Mebos, in 1992, the director was Prca Zvonko, from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the president of the executive board of the Mebos factory was Delic Dragan, a Muslim from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the fact that Fitozovic Smail, an economist from Samac, was a reserve captain of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly he was, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you aware of the fact that Mr. Fitozovic Smail was also tasked by the SDA and the party armed formation of SDA with an automatic weapon called Zagi?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: We established yesterday that this witness says that he knew nothing about the existence of armed formations of the SDA. He said he knows about some self-organised groups but nothing of an armed faction of the SDA, and that was made clear on the record yesterday, twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: As you went with Mr. Smail Fitozovic, you were guard, neighbourhood guards, did Mr. Smail Fitozovic, on those occasions, did he carry an automatic weapon called Zagi?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never carried any automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you and Mr. Smail Fitozovic went in these patrols with your hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When you went into these neighbourhood patrols, did you carry carabines or the shotgun?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I carried a shotgun, and Smail Fitozovic had nothing on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Smail Fitozovic was a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I don't think that he was a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask again to present to the witness in evidence D25 ter, 25/4 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I would kindly ask you to look at the attachment 9/1. Please glance through this document. Can you confirm the logistics base and the commander Fitozovic Smail?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And can we agree that all the names appearing on this attachment are persons of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, can you tell us: When did Alija Fitozovic talk to you? And you will find that in item -- under item 30 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: When did this talk take place, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I cannot tell you, but I did mention that the talk took place --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: It's not a contentious matter, this item, but I'm only interested when did this talk take place between you and Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, you may assist the witness if you relate in connection with certain events perhaps before this event or after this event, to try and assist the witness to remember. Because he did say previously that he can't remember dates. It's been a long time. So if it's important to you, perhaps you can help him by suggesting between which events. Perhaps he can remember. Generally the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, would you say that it did happen in 1991?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it did not occur then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we can agree that it was -- took place in 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that I cannot determine exactly 1991 or 1992, but I cannot say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it maybe after or before that rally and the meeting in the local commune which was presided over by Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recollect whether it was prior to or after that. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you refused this proposal of his?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would ask you to look at the same document, D25/4 ter, to find the attachment 4.2/.2.2. Did you find it? Look at it. Please get acquainted with the document, see the title, and then I'll ask you a question about it. Can you confirm that we have the anti-sabotage unit and number 5 we have the name of Jasarevic Osman, in brackets, Roma, with the telephone 61-917?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is your nickname Roma?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember whether this was your telephone number in 1991, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says "750," but that's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Under your -- next to your name, we have 61-917.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 61-917. And it's been added "arrested."

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I was only interested in the telephone number, 61-917. You don't have your glasses. Maybe that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And were all the members on this list members of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it is time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. How much more time do you need, Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I'll need at least another two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a long time. Because the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I agree that it's a long time, but in the statement there are matters which have not been raised. I don't know why we have this -- such a statement. There are many questions, many items, which have to be cleared up. Quite possibly it will be shorter than that, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please do reorganise your cross-examination during the break and try to concentrate on matters attaching the defence of your client, Mr. Pisarevic. Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, can I just confirm that today we would have the complete afternoon session, that we go up to a quarter to 2.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, you mean we shall sit the normal hours? Yes, we'll go the normal hours today.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we'll take our break and continue at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, let us clarify something in the transcript. My question was: Is your phone number - and I'm speaking about the year 1991 and 1992 - 61-917?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now ask you to refer to attachment 4, item 4. Would you be kind enough to browse through this document, familiarise yourself with this document, please, and then I'll put one question to you with regard to this document. Can you confirm that on this document, which is entitled, "Engineering sabotage detachment, department for special purposes," under item G6 we can find the names of Tihic Pasaga under 1, Jasarevic Osman under 2 and Seljakovic Hajrudin under 3? Did I read these names correctly?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Under 2, Jasarevic Osman, this is you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This is your phone number?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I no longer need this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to go to your written statement and to focus on item 33. Please find the relevant item and read it out on both pages, because it is on two pages in your language. Here you stated that on the way back you met Simo Zaric, Fadil Topcagic, a man called Dzuheric, aka Coc. This was around 7.00 p.m. Is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: However, nowhere in the statement did you state -- the statement, that is, that you gave to the Prosecutor's office on the 3rd, the 4th, and the 5th of February, 1995 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could my learned friend confirm this fact and spare me with the request for the witness to read this statement aloud?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Is counsel asking the Prosecution to stipulate that nowhere in the statement of 1995 is that same statement contained? Is that it, that same sentence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what counsel is asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't see it here, but I haven't -- counsel never said that he was going to ask me that -- ask me to stipulate on anything, so all I can tell the Bench is I don't see it in front of me now as I read the statement. I can only assume that the witness wasn't asked about it at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What counsel is asking is that what he referred to in P129 --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- does not appear in the statement of 1995 made by this witness; that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Your Honour, what I've said to you is that as far as I can see from glancing through it, it doesn't appear to be. I was not put on notice by counsel about being asked to stipulate on anything, so I haven't read it carefully in detail to check. But from what I -- I'm looking at the paragraphs that relate to the 16th of April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps it will be easier if counsel just asks the witness directly whether he stated whatever information you want to compare his evidence with in the statement of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. I have in front of me the witness's statement, which says that on the 16th of April he returned to Gradacac, and in this item he describes his return to Samac, and he never mentions ever seeing, then, Mr. Simo Zaric. I assume that the witness does not know his statement by heart. I have a copy of his statement, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now that counsel has, for the first time, said he wants us to confirm things, I've read that page. It's page 3. And -- sorry. It's page 4. ERN number 00258309. And I can confirm that on that page which I've read, the sentence about seeing Simo Zaric does not appear, and I think that's as far as we can go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pisarevic, that's satisfactory?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm satisfied, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you, sir, to proceed to item 38. Here you stated that on the way to your mother's house, you went by the city centre --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, the evidence is already there on record. Do not repeat it. Just ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to help the witness, to put him into the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that only a smaller section of the town, in which the police building is located and the building of the municipal commune and the part of eastern Mahala, at that time, on the 17th of February [as interpreted], 1992, was under the control of the Serb forces, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the monuments house. And the second exit to Samac was also blocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: To my knowledge, you did not go towards the second exit, towards the church --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Towards Crkvina. Correction of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date is not correct here in the transcript. I didn't say 17th of February. My date was the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can we agree that we were talking about the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You did not answer my question whether a major part of Bosanski Samac, the local commune, was under the control of the members of the armed unit of the SDA for the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I finish the sentence, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's mentioned already members of the armed unit of the SDA. This witness has now testified yesterday and today about no knowledge of armed units attached specifically to the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. Will you please remember that? We can't go on reminding you. It may be the case for the Defence, but certainly this witness has not given any evidence to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I'll rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness, these armed civilians, you referred to them as members of the Territorial Defence, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: On what grounds, and how do you know that these were members of the Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no other units in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, you stated that they had no uniforms, no insignia, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see this Territorial Defence unit? Did you ever see the list of the members of this unit?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You told me that you saw Nusret Kapetanovic and Suad Dumonjic [Realtime transcript read in error "Djuheric"] carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you, in addition to these two persons --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've just been suggested that the name Suad Dumanjic, Suad Dumanjic is the correct name of the person concerned. Could this be corrected please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. It's corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Djakic Damir?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mentioned the persons that I did see in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you neither saw Srna Salko, nor Jasarevic Muharem, nor Fadil Jasarevic, Mehinovic Kemal?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You also didn't see Bicic Hasan, Bicic Muhamed, Dagovic Esad, Dagovic Safet, Salkic Ibrahim, aka Ibela, or Pasaga Tihic? You didn't see these persons?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I just saw the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to me that Suad Dumanjic and Nusret Kapetanovic are of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions that have to do with item 43. Would you please go through item 43 of your written statement. Witness, can you tell me when and to whom did you return your automatic rifle belonging to the family of Kalashnikovs?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned my hunting rifle, a carbine and a shotgun, and I turned them over, together with the weapons permit, as I stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, this is not disputable. My question was as follows: When and to whom did you return the automatic rifle that you had received from Srna Safet?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Jasarevic has said -- I apologise. Mr. Pisarevic, counsel, said: I want to ask you about item 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: He's not asking about item 43. He's asking about item 28, where the witness says that he returned it immediately and only had it for 24 hours. So I don't know where Mr. Pisarevic is going with this, but it's contrary to the paragraph he indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question that I raised in connection with item 43 has to do with the fact that we have information, we've received information that Mr. Jasarevic, on that very day, in addition to the hunting weapon that he had mentioned, also returned a Kalashnikov automatic rifle. This is why I first wanted to find out when he returned it. Had he answered this question, I wouldn't have proceeded to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. When you have information according to your instructions which is not contained in any of the statements of the witness, please say so, that according to your instructions, this is what transpired. And then you ask him to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your instruction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, on the basis of our information, together with your hunting weapons, you returned to the police who came also a Kalashnikov automatic rifle, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. I turned over to them only my hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when and to whom?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is stated in my statement to whom; however, I do not know exactly the date. I also know that it was Safet Srna who came and gave me the rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did that happen three months prior to the outbreak of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I do not know exactly the time when this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall now proceed to another topic. It has to do with item 47 of your written statement. Here you stated that you were arrested on Sunday, April 20th.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Given the fact that the year is not stated here, could you confirm that you were arrested on the 20th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us at what time on the 20th of April, 1992 you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours. This is what also is stated in my statement. After lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours. Could that be around 1600 hours?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, is it important for the hour to be specified? Is it not sufficient that it was in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for my line of defence and for my analysis of this very crucial day, April 20th, the time schedule is also important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If you have instructions that it was a particular hour, put it to the witness, because he has stated in his evidence when he was arrested. So just put it directly to the witness: According to your instructions, it was such-and-such an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are not my instructions, because I do not know when he was arrested. This is why, through my questions to the witness, I'm trying to find out when he was arrested. The afternoon hours is a rather lengthy period of time. I would therefore have to ask, then, the witness: When did you take your lunch? How long did you take a nap? So I will ask the witness to tell me whether it was at around 2.00 p.m., 3.00 p.m., 4.00 p.m. If he can't do it, of course we will proceed to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness has said that he can't remember the exact time; it was in the afternoon. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Item 51 of your written statement contains your statement that you were taken to the SUP building. If you can recall it, could you tell this Honourable Chamber where in the police station you established, for the first time, your contact with Mr. Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the hall of the police station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it on the ground floor, in the hall, in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think it was on one of the floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a mistake, Your Honour, here in the transcript; therefore, I'll put my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, Witness, that the police station in Samac only has a ground floor and one floor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you established a contact with Stevan Todorovic. Your first encounter was on the first floor, wasn't it, the only floor that existed in the police station in Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In item 53, would you please have a look at this item of your written statement. You stated that you were taken to the floor, to another room. Do I understand it correctly that from the ground floor you were taken to a first floor, or were you taken direct to a room on the floor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Once you have been -- you were beaten in the corridor, you were just taken to a room on the floor? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This is where you were put in front of a table and some ten men wearing camouflage uniforms and camouflage paint were beating you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was the door to this room closed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now proceed to item 56. Now, can you tell me: Where is the room located with cells in the SUP building in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the side of the garages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this room on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is on the first floor. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the room you were referring to was located, the one with Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When in my statement, I said that they started beating me in the corridor, next to an upholstered door on the first floor. The door was broken through. And this is what I said in my written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown Exhibit P14, photograph 52, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P14A?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please place the photo on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please look carefully at this photo. Is this -- this room and the cells where you were locked up?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the cells were like this. But it's not that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are these the cells?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cells were like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the bars on this window?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
