utterances.text: You can see also these pipes of the central heating system going towards the ceiling and upwards to the floor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If you look more carefully through the picture and through the window, you will see a roof, something like that.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Also in that room you were talking about, on the floor, and that such cells existed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And did the -- were the windows covered with such bars?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember of a window. I was immediately placed into this cell. I was all bloodied. They pulled me by the hair and -- well, I couldn't look at a window.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If you remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask that the witness be shown, from P14, the photograph F53.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, look at this photo. Can you confirm for us that this is a photo of the police station in Samac, from the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you, on this photograph, on the floor, see, anywhere, the -- any bars?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was imprisoned here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have to wonder again about wasting time going down this area. The witness has said the cells were like, the ones in picture 52, the cells were like the ones he was held in, but it was not that room. He said that clearly. He then said, he doesn't remember window or he just remembers there were bars because of the circumstances. So I don't see how it follows on now to ask if he sees bars on this picture, because the witness has said that whether that relates to his room or not is not something within his memory and that photograph 52, to his memory, is not the room, although it was those kinds of cells that he was thrown into. So I really am anxious not to waste too much time. And perhaps no probative matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we claim -- we claim that on the floor, such cells did not exist, and that is the reason that we showed the witness the photograph, so that in order to show him that these bars don't exist. We, on the basis of evidence presented, and hearing witnesses who really stayed in these cells and went through the entire police station, we know that cells existed only on ground floor. However, I will show no other photos to the witness. I just wanted to confirm -- for him to confirm that this is the police station, the backside of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, the next question is whether the door in that room where the cells were, did the door exist? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that the cells were in a room.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I am asking whether there was a door, the entrance to this room.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were they -- could they be locked?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cells could be locked, the cells where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, Madam President Mumba said -- told you to answer the question. I asked you whether the doors of the room were being locked.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I said the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Only the cells were locked?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who had the keys of those cells?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who had the key.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you see from the cell -- from one cell to another cell?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You, in item 57, you described that on that evening certain people came, they got out of the cell. Where did they beat you when they got you out of the cell?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what time it was at night?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it was. I know that when I was moved, transferred to the TO, it was already dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When they beat you, was it already dark?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: But you said it was dark.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also said it in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Were the lights on? Was there any electricity in that police station on that night?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you, from this cell where you were located -- could you see the hall?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the final cell, and I could only see -- I could see into the hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they beat you and Mr. Izet Izetbegovic at the same time then?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They pulled us both from our cells.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they beat you both then?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they beat Izet Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You could see that Izet Izetbegovic was beaten, and could he see you being beaten?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was -- after he was returned to his cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: From his cell, could he see or recognise that you were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: All this was happening on the 20th of April, 1992, in the evening hours, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date the.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: But that was on the day that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. Oh, yes. I was just wondering whether you had finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will conclude rapidly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw an upholstered door. Was it written on the door that this is the office of Mr. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing was written on it, but I heard Simo's voice and I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that. Can you tell us just to what extent was this door open?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About ten centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did this door open? Towards the interior of the room or towards the corridor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Jasarevic, you, in your statement which you have given on the basis of recollection and knowledge, on the 3rd, 4th, and 5th of February, 1995, in describing this beating, in not in any moment did you ever mention Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask the Prosecution to get acquainted with the statement of the witness and whether they can confirm that in his statement he did not mention the name of Simo Zaric in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, well, that's not the case, because Simo Zaric is mentioned in the statement. What I can say for the record is that I've read quickly through page 6, ERN 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When he was describing this beating, the beating on the day he was arrested, that is what the counsel's question is related to.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's why I read this page, but that's -- his actual question is phrased in such a way to cover the whole statement. So from my answer, I'd just like to clarify that on page 00258311, in which the beating is talked about, I do not see in a brief looking over it, the name of Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understood correctly, the Prosecution -- well, in the description of this event, the name of Simo Zaric is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned it in all my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that two local Serbs were present: Milos Culapovic, known as Culap, and Savo Cancarevic, the commander of the police; isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: However, you've never mentioned Simo Zaric within that.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I also described our talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In view of this claim of yours that you mentioned Mr. Simo Zaric, I have to give you your statement in order that you can read this paragraph marked with a Roman X, so that you can get acquainted with it and to tell us whether you really stated this and if it is your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, this question you are trying to put to the witness, is it still in relation to the beating on the day he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To say that when he described the event in that statement, he did not mention the name of Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness can answer, after looking at the paragraph where he describes the beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: After reading it, just tell me when you've read it.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here it says nothing in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please return this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And now I would ask you -- I have -- there's another matter I'd like to clear up with you. Please look at item 57. Here you describe that they forced you to swim in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Which paragraph? Excuse me. Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, paragraph 57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, but in the English translation, there is not a word.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. 59. 59, but I will link it up, connect it with paragraph 57. That is why this mistake occurred at the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you look, Witness, at paragraph 59?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did, on that occasion, did somebody mention to you that you in the past stated that Serbs will be swimming, floating down the Sava River?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never made such a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, Mr. Jasarevic, in the factory where you worked, the Mebos factory, when Stojan Blagojevic placed on the bulletin board in the factory plant, Mebos, in the plant for the maintenance -- tools and maintenance department, he placed on the bulletin board the electoral poster of SDS -- did you, in front of several workers, broke that bulletin board, namely, the glass pane on it, ripped this poster, electoral poster, and said that this is how the Serbs will be swimming down the river?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true, I did take down that poster, but I never stated that the Serbs would be swimming down river Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, this act of yours, did it cause resentment of all the workers there, both Muslims, Croats, and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No party posters were allowed within the factory walls, and that was the decision taken in the factory, and that was the reason that the poster was taken down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you, in that moment of time -- were you considered as a person who has an expressly anti-Serb attitude?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to paragraph 85. This is the paragraph describing your transfer to Brcko. Can you recall that the transfer to Brcko was carried on the 26th of April, 1992, at night?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that in the TO, where the detainees were, that in addition to Simo Zaric, Mihaljo Topolovac also entered it, and that on that occasion Simo Zaric turned to the people and addressed with a few words to the people there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on that occasion he stated -- he stated: "I have to tell you something quickly, namely, that for your personal security and all that is happening here, and the position you're in, it's been decided that you be transferred to a safe place"? And next, that on that occasion he also stated: "Please don't ask me anything, because it is in your interest to move you from here as quickly as possible."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement was, as I heard it, that we'd be moving to another place for reasons of security, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask you to look at page 95 -- paragraph, paragraph - I apologise - paragraph 95. Mr. Jasarevic, we are skipping these statements that you had a doctor, that you could have a shower, and so on. We won't lose time on that. But here I would like to ask you: In your earlier statement, you said that on -- you've seen Mr. Nikolic in Brcko on the 27th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date, but I saw him then, in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the lieutenant colonel introduce himself when you came there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not introduce himself, but the captain with a cast told me to go and see Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of that information, you concluded that the officer was Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had these ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever know -- were you acquainted with Captain Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The person who was in the garrison in Brcko, did he introduce himself as Captain Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I thought he was Filipovic. I saw him with a cast in Samac, and he was with a cast when he took me to see Nikolic. This is what is contained in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about Captain Petrovic, because according to our information and the instructions I have, it's claimed that it wasn't Colonel Nikolic but that it was Lieutenant Colonel Petrovic [as interpreted] who was with Mr. Topcagic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't have the rank of a captain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the answer be cleared? Who didn't have the rank of captain? No. I'm asking the witness, because he's the one who answered he didn't have the rank of captain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person having a rank of captain was the person who brought me to the office of Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just a point for clarification. On page 54, in your question line 17 to 19, there is some confusion on the first line you are talking about Captain Petrovic, and on the third line you are saying Lieutenant Colonel Petrovic. His rank was captain, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. These are different persons. Captain Petrovic, not the person who brought in this witness or told him. My -- according to my information, Mr. Jasarevic was brought in by Captain Nebojsa Panjatovic, and he was the person with a plaster cast. He -- the witness thought it was Filipovic, but according to our information it was Nebojsa Penjatovic. The question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. You didn't understand my intervention, whether two persons by the name of Petrovic, one Captain Petrovic and a Lieutenant Colonel Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Petrovic is captain, and Mr. Stevan Nikolic is the lieutenant colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. So there is some mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: There is a mistake in the transcript. There is no such person as Lieutenant Colonel Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, sir, there is no such person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, do you allow for the possibility that on that occasion, in the Brcko garrison, when you were talking with Topcagic, Stanisic, and Zaric, Captain Petrovic and not Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic was present?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A person with a plaster cast took me to Colonel Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have only a few questions for you, Witness. Fadil Topcagic, like Fatima Saric [phoen], are your relatives, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Since you stated this in the course of one of your -- of the cross-examinations, you said that Fadil said that he will hide you for a while. Could you explain to us what did in fact Fadil have in mind? How would he hide you? How -- from whom would he hide you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know from whom he was supposed to hide me. I wasn't really listening to him. I was in such a state that I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you didn't understand him well?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even ask him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that Simo Zaric promised to your aunt that he will return you to Samac; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Your aunt is this Sanija Jasarevic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Ceribasic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This aunt of yours is the sister of your mother, isn't she?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that she died? Don't you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that Mr. Simo Zaric attended her funeral?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was there. He could go there. I couldn't go there. And her son was also at that ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Your brother, Hasan Jasarevic, having been released from Batkovici, left for Serbia, for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went for Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: But before he left for Germany, he went to Serbia and/or the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Your mother's name was Satka, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Your sister, who was together with your mother, was Fata, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And your sister had a son who was a student?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that they also left for Serbia and that for a short period of time they stayed in the Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to pay for false personal documents, the identity card. They had to pay 500, 600 Deutschmark for each document, and they left under false names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that they left for Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all left for Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: May I just point out to Mr. Pisarevic that this is contained in paragraph 128 of his statement that his mother and his sister left in that way and went out through Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, they went to Germany through Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It says in the statement they went through Serbia. So I am anxious for this witness could be released by the end of today. So if it's in the statement, I think it's perhaps unnecessary to have it repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is what is said in the statement, but it doesn't say only through Serbia, and my line of questions aimed at the following question:

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, Witness, are you familiar with the fact that your mother, your sister, and your cousin in Belgrade at the railway station, were received by Paunovic Branko, Badza [phoen], Mr. Zaric, and his wife Faketa? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Faketa was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that your mother, Satka, sister Fata, and your cousin were accommodated at Bezanija, in Belgrade, with Simo Zaric's mother-in-law and/or the mother of Fadil Topcagic, Djula, Fadil's wife Dina, and Fadil's children?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My cousin was not there. My mother and sister were there. They stayed at Djula's.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that together with them, for more -- they stayed for more than one month with them?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long, but something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that their food and other supplies required for their life and maintenance of Djula, Dina, and your mother and your sister, were provided for and brought in by Simo Zaric and Fadil Topcagic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Fadil, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. I have only one more question for you, Witness. Is the information true that the flat you have in Samac was put on sale? Did you let people know that you planned to leave Samac, that you would ask for asylum [Realtime transcript read in error "a^"] in Germany? Yes or No?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. This is why I came back to Samac when I had received the flat. My mother had even received the house two months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have finished with my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one short intervention to the transcript here in page 59, line 14, he was asking for asylum in Germany. Here it's just letter "a", so it's just clarification. And the witness answered already to that question. He heard it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That is corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Could I ask if the number of documents that were shown to the witness could be shown again. I'll start with perhaps document D14/4. I believe it's a list of names. Yes

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, the question that was never put to you: Have you ever seen this document before you arrived here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never have I seen this list, or any other list, nor has anybody shown me a list like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say no one has shown you a list, that includes your whole time in detention, nothing like this was ever put to you, was it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never have I been shown a list also while I was in detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever give permission to anyone to put your name on such a list?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never gave either permission or my signature on any list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown D25/4. May I just see the document for a minute? I hope I've asked for the right exhibit number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I'd like to ask you to look at what's called attachment 4.4. I think we've established your name is at G6.2. Have you ever seen this document before walking into this courtroom here today?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see this list before.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When did you see this list?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, in the course of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You're -- absolutely. You were shown this in the cross-examination. Was that the first time you had seen this list, when it was put to you by Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first time that I was shown this list is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you ever at any time a member of an engineering and sabotage platoon?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it in my statement, that I had an informal discussion with Alija Fitozovic, but I turned it down, the offer, immediately and flatly, and I never was a member of any organisation of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: For the sake of thoroughness, Mr. Jasarevic, I'd just like to ask you: Were you ever asked about your role in this platoon, or was this list ever put to you at any stage during your detention in 1992 in Bosanski Samac? Can you just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. No list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, just for clarity's sake: Mr. Pisarevic also asked you to have a look at -- I'm sorry. Just let me -- it's attachment 4.2. And Mr. Jasarevic, is it the same circumstances with this list as with the other, that you've seen it for the first time here when you came to testify and that at no stage during your detention was this list ever shown to you or were you ever asked about any alleged involvement in anti-sabotage section?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never asked, nor was I ever shown any list during my detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'd now like the witness to be shown D38/1. And perhaps you could bring D39/1 with you as well. It might speed things up. And D35/1. They were the three that Mr. Pisarevic used. D35/1, D38/1 and D39/1. Perhaps we'll just go in sequential order. If D35/1 could be shown to the witness first.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, you were never again asked about this list. Had you ever, ever seen this list before Mr. Pisarevic showed it to you on the stand here?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never shown this list before, at any point in time, apart from this cross-examination here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were detained in Bosanski Samac, were you ever questioned at all about being issued with a Kalashnikov and some ammunition and a number of clips of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody questioned me about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown number 38/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this list?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this list either.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know anything about this list? Have you heard about it, anybody informed you of its existence?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never informed about it or about the existence of any list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown D39/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, for the record, before you were asked questions by Mr. Pisarevic, had you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had never seen this list before Mr. Pisarevic showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Had anyone ever asked you about going out in a group 4 with two other persons, one called Pasaga Tihic and one called Hajrudin Seljakovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody asked me about this list or this group.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: At no time during your detention were you ever asked any questions on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They never questioned me about this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever go on patrol with Mr. Tihic -- this is Pasaga Tihic or Mr. Hajrudin Seljakovic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never went with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You did go out on these neighbourhood patrols with Smail Fitozovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you have a quick look through the names here? Perhaps it's easier for you to look at the actual document and see whether you see his name there.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see on this list Fitozovic Smail.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm finished with that document. Could I ask if the witness could be shown document 36 -- D36/1. It's not one yet put to the witness by Mr. Pisarevic, but it's all part of the same kind of documentation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, could you just take a minute or two to familiarise yourself with this document, and just for your own sake, perhaps the original is easier. For the record, this is a handwritten document which is called "Persons who received payment for being on duty from the 3rd to the 7th of March" and "Persons who received payments for being on duty from the 8th to the 13th of March," both -- well, the second one is certainly 1992. Mr. Jasarevic, could I ask you, in familiarising yourself with that document, whether you can see your name in it for having received any payment for being on duty?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever participate in a formal patrol or group such as the types you've seen put to you on the list and did you ever receive payment for your participation in these neighbourhood watches?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never -- I never received any payment, I never saw this list. I already stated that I went only together with Smail Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I've finished with that document. Since we started with cross-examination by Mr. Pisarevic, I'll continue with issues raised by him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: He raised an incident where you had removed an SDS electoral poster from the factory where you worked. Were there SDA and HDZ electoral posters up in the factory?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated, it was prohibited for any poster to be put up, and no one else put any other poster there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Another part of Mr. Pisarevic's cross-examination was to ask you about an alleged statement taken from you by Inspector Savic. Now, we don't have a copy of this document and have no knowledge that it actually exists, but did you ever say to Mr. Savic, as far as you can remember, that you used to be a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it before: I was forced to say that. There was no choice. I didn't have any choice. I was told that I should state that I was a member, but -- and I had to sign it as well. Whatever they insisted for me to do, I did it, and I would have signed anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall take our break for 20 minutes. We shall resume our proceedings at 1250 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, Mr. Pisarevic asked you about several incidents involving his client, which he said you did not mention in the statement you gave to the OTP in February of 1995. Do you know that the indictment in this case was issued in June 1995, after you had given your statement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It's I think in fact a public knowledge that the indictment was originally issued in June. So when we in fact met in May of this year, was that the first time that someone from the Office of the Prosecutor specifically asked you about the presence of these defendants in the SUP building whilst you were being beaten in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Is that nobody prior to when we met this year, in May, was I the first person to ask you whether any of the defendants were in the SUP building when you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until then, nobody had posed that question to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jasarevic, could I also ask you to confirm that your information about your meeting in Brcko between yourself, Colonel Nikolic, and Mr. Zaric was also in your statement of February 1995? If I tell you that it's here, would you accept that as true?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it true that also at that time you stated how you had been offered your freedom in exchange for joining the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. While we're on the matter of the 4th Detachment, this morning Mr. Pisarevic asked you about an incident in which he referred to civilians who were injured. Is it correct that all those civilians were also members of the 4th Detachment? Do you know the incident I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, and they were all members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when they said they were civilians, they were all members of the 4th Detachment, were they all also armed at the time, to the best of your information?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked questions about your sister and mother going through Germany -- going through Serbia. Is it correct that they purchased forged documents in order to do that, what Mr. Pisarevic was asking you about?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had to get forged documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And they paid money for those forged documents?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the documents had to be paid, as well as the transportation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know who they had to pay all this money to? Were you ever told?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who they paid the money to?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the ID, I do not know. Srdic and a former policeman, a retired policeman, and for my mother and sisters, Ignjo Popovic ensured the transport.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that your family left Bosanski Samac in this manner because they could not be exchanged. Could you explain what you mean by "they could not be exchanged"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not that anybody could just apply and go for the exchange. It wasn't like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be worthwhile clarifying when this happened, the period of time, concerning what has been stated by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After 17 months.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Witness, -- sorry, Mr. Jasarevic. 17 months after what?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the fall of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So 17 months after the fall of Bosanski Samac your mother and sisters left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could they not leave of their own free will, if that was their desire? Why did they have to buy forged documents?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with their true documents, they couldn't leave, because they had Muslim names.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So their whole movement and everything was completely controlled, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that there is calling for some conclusions and speculation from this witness. He wasn't present there, so there is no basis for this kind of question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. And also sometimes when you are re-examining, please deal with matters that are relevant to the indictment, not just any question that was raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Because one of -- two of the counts in the indictment relate to deportation, the manner in which people went in and out of Samac is something I'd like to touch on since counsel raised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes but in this particular case the family and relatives of this particular witness, as Mr. Lazarevic says, he was not present when the events in question are being raised -- happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. He does, however, have information which he's provided and which Mr. Pisarevic asked him about, for example, where they stayed in Serbia and how long.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I'll finish this topic in a minute. I just am seeking a clarification on your answer, which was that because they had Muslim documents -- because -- sorry. Here is your answer. You said: "With their true documents, they couldn't leave, because they had Muslim names." Would you just explain what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The true documents, on the true documents, Muslim names were written on them, and nobody could get out with Muslim names and to go from there to Serbia, and they had to go because there was a commission in Bosanski Samac which entered the homes, and they would make a report of the property, and that would imply that you'd be evicted, taken out of your house, and sent to the Zasavica camp. And Vajagic Joka was at the head of that commission and that was the reason that they had to leave Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also questioned at length about the weapon you were issued with and exactly what type of weapon it was. At any stage was an illegal weapon ever found on your person or in your home in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing illegal was ever found on me personally or in my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was an allegation ever put to you whilst you were in detention that such an illegal automatic weapon was ever found on your person or in your home, or indeed anywhere where it was indicated that the automatic weapon was yours?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was never found. I never had it and it was never in my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now move on to the examination by counsel for Mr. Tadic. And you were being asked about the exchange of your mother-in-law, and you said that you believed it was in the last exchange, and I'm going to quote from the transcript. You said: "It was an elderly woman, 70-odd years, from Zasavica, Zasavica camp. She was transferred. Nobody asked where she will be going." Could I ask you to explain what you mean by the fact that she was transferred and nobody asked where she will be going?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She wanted to go home. Nobody asked her, so she had to go into the exchange because her apartment was already occupied.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And this information from having spoken with your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. From the conversation I had with my mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You also used the word in your earlier answer about the fact that she was transferred. Do you have any information as to whether people were exchanged at the time she was or whether she was just taken to the border or to a demarcation line and left there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was taken from Zasavica to the place where the exchange took place, like everybody else who were in Zasavica, from Zasavica, and who were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And do you have any information whether or not, like in your exchange, people came from the other side into Serb-controlled areas, or whether in fact she and other people with her were just placed -- you said brought to the -- to that designated place and handed over to the other side, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On -- the civilians weren't taken across to the other side, but only prisoners of war, and from Samac only civilians were taken across.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you say "prisoners of war," what --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What do you mean? Were they people in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not in uniforms. I saw younger men.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you present at the exchange of your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to -- also on the matter of exchanges, you were asked about your activity on the Croatian side, and you had said that you went to international organisations about your wife and children. Could you just tell us for the record what sort of international organisations those were?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were various organisations for the reunionification of families: The International Red Cross, the local Red Cross. These were the organisations I visited.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, did you go and visit these organisations because your wife, of her own free will, could not be reunited with her -- sorry. That your wife was not free to be reunited with you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the reason I went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to move on, finally, to the cross-examination. I believe it was already at this stage by Mr. Novic on behalf of Blagoje Simic, and you were asked about the gathering three days -- three days after the takeover of Samac, the gathering outside the Territorial Defence building, because there had been an announcement for people to report there. And you said that whoever moved -- that you saw people with white armbands on them, the Muslims and the Croats, and whoever moved about had to wear a white armband. Is it the case that there was an announcement that Muslims and Croats were told that when they went out, that they should wear a white armband? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this order was issued, to wear white armbands, but I do know that everybody was wearing them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked also by counsel about checkpoints, and as you said in your statement, that there were also checkpoints in Croatian villages. Now, I just want to clarify something in the transcript so it can't be used against you. You were asked to say which villages the checkpoints were set up in, and you mentioned Hasici, Domaljevac, Crkvina, and Serbian Tisina. Is it correct that Hasici and Domaljevac are Croat villages?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Crkvina and Serbian Tisina are Serb-populated villages?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So in your answer, you were referring in general to where checkpoints were, not just Croat ones or not just Serb ones?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, do you have your statement in front of you, the one that is in evidence here before this Court? Yes? If you look at paragraph 21, you'll see your statement says: "There were some checkpoints in Croatian villages, including Hasici." And then the statement says Domaljevac didn't have a checkpoint. Is that correct or is it your recollection that there was a checkpoint at Domaljevac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the checkpoint myself, but I heard that it exists.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This is the checkpoint at Domaljevac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's the end of that matter. You were also questioned by the same counsel about hearing of the establishment of the Aleksandar Vukovic Foundation by the Crisis Staff of Samac over Radio Samac, and you told counsel that: "I always listened to the radio, because Simo Zaric had a show, a programme in which he daily spoke about how Muslim and Croat forces had been preparing an attack on Samac and who ever's name he mentioned on the radio was arrested. That happened to my brother." Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you hear these announcements when you were already exchanged in Orasje, whilst you were in Orasje?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't arrive yet to Orasje when I heard this about my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Where were you when you heard the announcement about your brother?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sick, in Slavonski Samac, and I myself was listening to the radio there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And after you heard this announcement, your brother was arrested?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do believe that this particular episode is quite important. Could the witness say to us the period when he was in Slavonski Samac and when he came to Orasje. Because, as we well know, yesterday, after several questions of my co-counsel, he didn't recollect anything. Now he's refreshing memory, which I really am grateful for that. And now we can maybe have a more precise time period. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Ms. Reidy can deal with that, to specify the time of these movements of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I will try, Your Honour, but, with respect, this was during cross-examination by Mr. Pantelic. His co-counsel could have pursued this matter, and it's not the case that the witness denied a memory of this at all, he just simply wasn't pursued. But I'll ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, could you tell me, as best you can recall, when you were in Slavonski Samac recovering?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavonski?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. I think you said that you were sick in Slavonski Samac and that you were -- that's where you heard the announcement about your brother.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you tell us when this happened? Was this immediately after your exchange?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If you can tell us --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when my brother was arrested, because I only heard about it after the first exchange. But his name was broadcast over the radio, and he was arrested, but I don't know the exact day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you perhaps tell us if you can remember when it was that you were sick in Slavonski Samac, if in fact -- maybe our record is wrong. Were you sick at some stage in Slavonski Samac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was ill.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And if you can remember, could you tell us roughly when this was?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe mid-July, but I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since we will have no opportunity to re-cross this witness or things like that, I do believe that there is some misunderstanding here in this transcript that things were not quite clear to me. I still don't understand from this transcript, did the witness actually heard that his brother was arrested or he heard the actual broadcast, or what? Maybe -- just this is the only possibility that we can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Ms. Reidy --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mind clarifying things, but I would like to bear in mind that Mr. Zaric -- Mr. Pisarevic spent many hours cross-examining this witness after this had already been put on the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Jasarevic, could you just tell us what it was you heard on the radio. Did you hear Mr. Simo Zaric making announcements, talking about people, giving names of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He mentioned, in this one programme on the radio, that a special hunters' unit would be established, and my brother Hasan would be a part of this unit's command. And after this one programme, he was arrested and he was taken to Batkovici, to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So what you heard was the broadcast, you heard Mr. Simo Zaric speaking?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what you learned later was that your brother was arrested?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. First detained in Samac, maltreated, mistreated, and then -- just like me, and then taken to Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. These broadcasts of Mr. Zaric, you said they took place on a daily basis. Is that what you recall?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a particular time, but I don't know whether his broadcast was on a daily basis. But of course, I followed all the news programmes, yet I don't know exactly the hour and whether this was a daily broadcast. I myself, however, heard him say things around the establishment of this hunters' unit and about my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Mr. Zaric say on whose behalf or on what authority he was making such announcements?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was Serbian Radio Samac, but he didn't say on whose behalf he had been speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Mr. Zaric ever include in the programmes any information about things happening to persons of Muslim and Croat ethnicity, such as their detention, maltreatment, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never spoke about that on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Jasarevic, one last thing, because it has been put to you a number of times by counsel. Do you hold any anti-Serb sentiment, and particularly in 1992, when you were living in Bosanski Samac, did you have anti-Serb sentiments?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never held anti-Serb sentiments. Hasan's wife, my sister-in-law, is a Serb, and she is been living with my brother in Gradacac. They simply couldn't return to their home until two months ago. All my childhood friends were Serbs, of Serb background, and I never held any such sentiments that had been alleged concerning the Serbs or other ethnicities. I myself was an advocate of peace in my town.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's the end of my re-exam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Jasarevic, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. We are now finished with you. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's no other witness, is there?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And I know we only have 15 minutes left, but on that matter, just so it's on the record and counsel know as well: I was advised during the break that the flight of the witness has been a little bit delayed, so he will be arriving in, but I hope that we'll be able to finish the 92 bis procedure and disclose it to Defence counsel as soon as possible. But they were provided with a draft translation of the 92 bis statement this morning, our translator having worked through the night to provide that for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the other two witnesses who had visa problems will be rescheduled?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's right. They will appear after Witness A, because I've been led to believe that their visa problem is solved or in the process of being solved. They had to get new passports, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And that they're being flown out at the beginning of next week and they'll be here. Although, if I'm correct, we don't sit next Thursday and Friday, the 11th and 12th, because of the Plenary Session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The programme has been sent to everybody concerned, yes. Are there any other matters? The Defence? We shall adjourn and continue our proceedings on Monday at 0900 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of July, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
